newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila oil fund will deplete unless prices hiked-ERB.
newsitem.headline: Manila oil fund will deplete unless prices hiked-ERB.

text.p: The Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) said on Thursday the one billion peso Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) will be wiped out by year-end if domestic oil prices are not raised.
"We will have to authorise an increase possibly in December but not at this time," ERB chairman Bayani Faylona told Reuters.

"We are having second thoughts in asking the opinion of the Department of Justice on the validity of the oil price increases since if they oppose our decisions, they can go to the Court of Appeals," added Faylona.

The ERB decided to suspend the implementation of the oil price hike slated for November until the Justice Department gives its opinion on the automatic oil price formula. Faylona earlier said petrol prices would have to be raised by 30 centavos per litre on the average for November.
The formula, an interim mechanism prior to full oil industry deregulation next year, allowed monthly adjustments in domestic pump prices since August without the previously required public hearings.
Any increases above 50 centavos per litre of petroleum product was absorbed by the buffer fund.
Energy Minister Francisco Viray told reporters that without a price increase, the only recourse is for Congress to agree to budgetary allocation to cover the projected deficit.
Viray said the deficit of the fund will reach 1.1 billion pesos by mid-January if oil prices are not raised.
The Department of Energy said the one billion peso buffer fund was reduced to 771.7 million pesos as of end-September.
Faylona said that withdrawal from the buffer fund is estimated at 500 million pesos a month.

The projected deficit is on top of an existing 2.376 billion pesos which the fund owes the country's three oil refiners. The government has agreed in principle to settle the amount but no timetable has been specified.
The one billion pesos was contributed by the Philippine National Oil Co to the OPSF in August at the start of partial deregulation.
